mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as concerns about economic slowdown grow.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity is abundant and borrowing costs are low.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strong demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month during a period of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY) signals supply-side constraints, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as inflationary pressures and economic slowdown concerns mount.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and CPIAUCSL is above 2.5% YoY.
